papers.summary: Based on the analysis of 96 organizational innovation in healthcare (OIH) projects and 52 interviews conducted with project leaders initiating these innovations, this research identifies the phenomena underlying the genesis of OIHs. The results highlight the major role played by factors such as patient empathy, international inspiration, academic inspiration, technological inspiration, serendipitous encounters, and the desire for organizational transformation in driving the generation of OIHs. Furthermore, our findings emphasize the dual nature of the research and development process for these innovations, characterized as both ex nihilo and ex materia.

papers.summary: This article explores the dynamics of collaborative and participatory innovations in public health services using Chen et al.’s (2020) typology. Based on a mixed survey of projects awarded under the national “Droits des usagers de la santé” initiative, the study finds that user participation primarily generates operational and capacity-oriented innovations frequently involving external partnerships. The article concludes by suggesting avenues for enhancing full co-creation processes in public services to maximize public value.

papers.summary: Carbohydrate binding proteins (CBPs) are alluring and challenging targets in biology. CBPs achieve high-affinity interactions with their substrates through multivalent interactions with carbohydrates, often in branched, heterogeneous structures. Many cell recognition events and host-pathogen interactions are mediated by these carbohydrate-protein interactions. Therefore, the development of glycan-based mimics and disruptors of these interactions have applications in studying target CBPs, carbohydrate-based vaccines, immunomodulating agents, diagnostics, and therapeutics against cancer and other diseases.
